objective: Source-audit Linux fs-verity and adjacent kernel/runtime integrity mechanisms for a minimal F2 target-VPS exact-source/immutable-byte evidence primitive. Determine exactly what they prove, what they do not prove, filesystem/privilege/deployment costs, and whether a thinner clean-worktree plus consumed-byte receipt remains preferable.
hypothesis: fs-verity can cheaply strengthen F2 target-runtime source integrity by making admitted files content-authenticated and immutable after enablement, reducing post-admission mutation risk while preserving deterministic digest binding.
counterhypothesis: fs-verity adds filesystem/kernel/enablement complexity and still does not prove which bytes a process actually executed or read; a clean exact-source worktree/container plus loader-consumption receipts may provide the necessary evidence with less complexity.
